## Overview

`/v1/messages` now accepts anthropic-defined client tools (`bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, `memory_*`) by supplying their built-in schemas to the chat template; second work item of #64810. follows #64575, which rejected these with a named 400.

## Claims

- requests that declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}`, `text_editor_20250728` / `str_replace_based_edit_tool`, and so on no longer fail; the model sees a regular function tool and `tool_use` comes back under the name the client expects, so the client keeps running the tool as it does against the anthropic api.
- registered versions: `bash_20241022`, `bash_20250124` (`bash`); `text_editor_20241022`, `text_editor_20250124` (`str_replace_editor`, with `undo_edit`, inserted text in `new_str`); `text_editor_20250429`, `text_editor_20250728` (`str_replace_based_edit_tool`, no `undo_edit`, inserted text in `insert_text`); `memory_20250818` (`memory`).
- a registered type declared under the wrong name gets a named 400 (`tool type 'text_editor_20250728' must be named 'str_replace_based_edit_tool', got ...`).
- server tools (`web_search_*`, `code_execution_*`, ...), `computer_*` and unknown versions keep the named 400 from #64575.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestToolDefinitions
```

new tests per registered version check the converted chat request (function name, description, parameters, command enum, `tool_choice=auto`), the version-specific insert field, tool-level options like `max_characters` being accepted, the wrong-name reject, the reject list (web_search, code_execution, computer, unknown bash version) and that the schema isn't shared between requests. all of `tests/entrypoints/anthropic` that runs on cpu passes; the only failures (`TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_non_jinja_renderer`) fail the same way on main in my cpu-only env. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

## Details

- new `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/client_tools.py` holds a small registry keyed by the versioned type: expected name, a short description, and the input schema built from anthropic's documented parameters. `AnthropicTool`'s before-validator expands registered types into a normal tool (keeping the original `type`), so `_convert_tools`, `tool_addition` and count_tokens all work unchanged.
- a client-supplied `description` is kept if present; the schema is deep-copied per request.
- tool-level options (`max_characters`) are accepted and ignored; vllm doesn't run the tool, so truncation stays on the client side.
- `computer_*` is left out on purpose: it needs display config and screenshot (image) tool results; happy to follow up separately.
- docs: added a note to `docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md`.

cc @robertgshaw2-redhat

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Built-in schemas for Anthropic-defined client tools.
+
+Anthropic-defined client tools (``bash_*``, ``text_editor_*``, ``memory_*``)
+are declared by a versioned ``type`` and a fixed ``name``, without an
+``input_schema``; the schema is built into Claude. The client still runs the
+tool, so vLLM only needs to hand the model an equivalent function schema and
+return ``tool_use`` blocks under the expected name.
+"""
+
+import copy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ClientToolSpec:
+    name: str
+    description: str
+    input_schema: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+def _object(properties: dict[str, Any], required: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {"type": "object", "properties": properties, "required": required}
+
+
+_BASH = ClientToolSpec(
+    name="bash",
+    description=(
+        "Run commands in a persistent bash shell session. State such as the "
+        "working directory and environment variables is kept between calls. "
+        "Set restart to true to restart the session."
+    ),
+    input_schema=_object(
+        {
+            "command": {
+                "type": "string",
+                "description": "The bash command to run.",
+            },
+            "restart": {
+                "type": "boolean",
+                "description": "Set to true to restart the bash session.",
+            },
+        },
+        [],
+    ),
+)
+
+_PATH = {
+    "type": "string",
+    "description": "Path to the file or directory.",
+}
+_VIEW_RANGE = {
+    "type": "array",
+    "items": {"type": "integer"},
+    "minItems": 2,
+    "maxItems": 2,
+    "description": (
+        "Optional [start, end] line range for view, 1-indexed; an end of -1 "
+        "reads to the end of the file."
+    ),
+}
+_FILE_TEXT = {"type": "string", "description": "Content of the file to create."}
+_OLD_STR = {"type": "string", "description": "Exact text to replace."}
+_NEW_STR = {"type": "string", "description": "Replacement text."}
+_INSERT_LINE = {
+    "type": "integer",
+    "description": "Line number after which to insert text; 0 inserts at the top.",
+}
+_INSERT_TEXT = {"type": "string", "description": "Text to insert."}
+
+
+def _text_editor(name: str, legacy: bool) -> ClientToolSpec:
+    commands = ["view", "create", "str_replace", "insert"]
+    properties: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "command": {"type": "string", "enum": commands},
+        "path": _PATH,
+        "view_range": _VIEW_RANGE,
+        "file_text": _FILE_TEXT,
+        "old_str": _OLD_STR,
+        "new_str": _NEW_STR,
+        "insert_line": _INSERT_LINE,
+    }
+    if legacy:
+        # The 2024-10-22 and 2025-01-24 editors take the inserted text in
+        # new_str and also support undo_edit.
+        commands.append("undo_edit")
+    else:
+        properties["insert_text"] = _INSERT_TEXT
+    return ClientToolSpec(
+        name=name,
+        description=(
+            "View, create and edit text files. view shows a file with line "
+            "numbers or lists a directory; create writes a new file; "
+            "str_replace replaces exactly one occurrence of old_str; insert "
+            "adds text after insert_line"
+            + ("; undo_edit reverts the last edit to path." if legacy else ".")
+        ),
+        input_schema=_object(properties, ["command", "path"]),
+    )
+
+
+_MEMORY = ClientToolSpec(
+    name="memory",
+    description=(
+        "Read and write files in a persistent /memories directory to keep "
+        "information across conversations."
+    ),
+    input_schema=_object(
+        {
+            "command": {
+                "type": "string",
+                "enum": [
+                    "view",
+                    "create",
+                    "str_replace",
+                    "insert",
+                    "delete",
+                    "rename",
+                ],
+            },
+            "path": _PATH,
+            "view_range": _VIEW_RANGE,
+            "file_text": _FILE_TEXT,
+            "old_str": _OLD_STR,
+            "new_str": _NEW_STR,
+            "insert_line": _INSERT_LINE,
+            "insert_text": _INSERT_TEXT,
+            "old_path": {"type": "string", "description": "Path to rename."},
+            "new_path": {"type": "string", "description": "New path."},
+        },
+        ["command"],
+    ),
+)
+
+CLIENT_TOOL_SPECS: dict[str, ClientToolSpec] = {
+    "bash_20241022": _BASH,
+    "bash_20250124": _BASH,
+    "text_editor_20241022": _text_editor("str_replace_editor", legacy=True),
+    "text_editor_20250124": _text_editor("str_replace_editor", legacy=True),
+    "text_editor_20250429": _text_editor("str_replace_based_edit_tool", legacy=False),
+    "text_editor_20250728": _text_editor("str_replace_based_edit_tool", legacy=False),
+    "memory_20250818": _MEMORY,
+}
+
+
+def expand_client_tool(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Return ``data`` with the built-in schema filled in, or ``None`` if
+    ``data`` is not a registered Anthropic-defined client tool."""
+    tool_type = data.get("type")
+    spec = CLIENT_TOOL_SPECS.get(tool_type) if isinstance(tool_type, str) else None
+    if spec is None:
+        return None
+    name = data.get("name")
+    if name != spec.name:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"tool type {tool_type!r} must be named {spec.name!r}, got {name!r}"
+        )
+    return {
+        **data,
+        "description": data.get("description") or spec.description,
+        "input_schema": copy.deepcopy(spec.input_schema),
+    }

@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator
 
 import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.entrypoints.anthropic.client_tools import expand_client_tool
 from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import (
     MMPayload,
     resolve_return_mm_kwargs_alias,
@@ -133,7 +134,9 @@ def validate_tool_change_role(self) -> "AnthropicMessage":
 class AnthropicTool(BaseModel):
     """Tool definition."""
 
-    type: Literal["custom"] | None = None
+    # "custom", or a registered Anthropic-defined client tool type such as
+    # "bash_20250124"; see client_tools.CLIENT_TOOL_SPECS.
+    type: str | None = None
     name: str
     description: str | None = None
     input_schema: dict[str, Any]
@@ -142,18 +145,24 @@ class AnthropicTool(BaseModel):
 
     @model_validator(mode="before")
     @classmethod
-    def reject_anthropic_defined_tools(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
-        # Anthropic-defined tools (web_search_*, code_execution_*, bash_*,
-        # text_editor_*, ...) carry a versioned ``type`` and no input_schema.
-        # Reject them by name here, before field validation would report a
-        # missing input_schema and point the client at the wrong problem.
+    def resolve_anthropic_defined_tools(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
+        # Anthropic-defined tools carry a versioned ``type`` and no
+        # input_schema. Client tools (bash_*, text_editor_*, memory_*) get
+        # their built-in schema filled in here; any other type (server tools
+        # such as web_search_*, or computer_*) is rejected by name before
+        # field validation would report a missing input_schema.
         if isinstance(data, dict):
             tool_type = data.get("type")
-            if tool_type not in (None, "custom"):
+            if tool_type in (None, "custom"):
+                return data
+            expanded = expand_client_tool(data)
+            if expanded is None:
                 raise ValueError(
                     f"tool type {tool_type!r} is not supported; only custom "
-                    "tools with an input_schema are supported"
+                    "tools with an input_schema and the Anthropic-defined "
+                    "bash, text_editor and memory client tools are supported"
                 )
+            return expanded
         return data
 
     @field_validator("input_schema")
